newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to prepare anti-inflation plan.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to prepare anti-inflation plan.

text.p: Hungary will work out a programme by the end of next month for reducing inflation, a government spokesman said on Sunday.

"The government decided that the finance minister...should work out a programme by the end of April about the reduction of the inflation rate," Elemer Kiss, secretary of state of the prime minister's office, told a news conference.
Kiss added that the programme would deal with a fight against inflation from next year onwards.
Hungary's inflation is running at 18.9 percent year-on-year. Average inflation was 23.6 percent in 1996.
According to the three-year economic guidelines approved by the government last year, Hungary planned to cut inflation by five percentage points every year between 1997 and 1999.

But urged on by the International Monetary Fund, the finance ministry said a month ago that it would prepare alternative draft budgets for 1998, with one of them targeting a larger-than-five-percent cut.
Analysts say the government will have difficulties if it tries to keep wage rises low for 1998, a year in which Hungary is likely to hold general elections.
